sources_considered.why: Original benchmark research documents false answers across several contemporary model families.
Read and confirmed the peer-reviewed publication; duplicates the research cited through its dated arXiv record.
Original research documents improved truthfulness, qualifying any assumption that contemporary models behaved identically.
Read to establish scope. It neither enumerates the models nor independently establishes their behavior.

evidence_items.publisher: Lin, Hilton and Evans; arXiv / ACL
evidence_items.explanation: The study evaluated GPT-3, GPT-Neo/J, GPT-2 and a T5-based model on questions designed to elicit common misconceptions. It establishes substantial false-answer rates on that benchmark, but neither identifies Marcus's complete model set nor measures ordinary-use fabrication frequency.

The researchers report improved truthfulness after training with human feedback. This qualifies comparisons across models and versions, but does not establish that any model Marcus saw rarely fabricated content.

unresolved_gaps: No complete, independently verifiable inventory of the models and versions Marcus had encountered was established.
The available benchmark does not establish fabrication frequency across his full set or across a specified ordinary-use prompt distribution.
